verification_result.summary: Structural findings are correct but the evaluation scope is too narrow. Focused only on existing data flow without testing the complete pipeline (36B → 30B → P-R-J → 27B → 32B). Missing: real extract output quality measurement, actual downstream verify costs, and comparison of different P-R-J model assignments.

reasoning: The 27B verify correctly identified the 7 structural issues and downgraded F03 severity appropriately. The operational impact assessment adds value. However, this evaluation is analyzing a pipeline that has only processed 4 turns — statistically insignificant. Key gaps: (1) No measurement of 3B retry cost — how many tokens are wasted on 3B double-failure before 30B fallback? (2) No measurement of how often the 30B fallback produces useful vs useless output. (3) No cost model comparison between '3B→30B fallback' and 'direct 30B extract' for long turns. (4) The evaluation doesn't test the P-R-J pipeline on extract results — it only analyzes data structures, not the review pipeline's ability to judge extract quality. Recommend a second round with: (a) larger sample (50+ turns), (b) direct 27B verify call via :8081, (c) cost token accounting for the 3B retry chain.

verification_items.detail: 6/7 genuine issues identified. F07 rejection is sound. However, 2 missing findings (see disagreements).

verification_items.check: Data source verification — actual extract data reviewed
verification_items.detail: 4 extract_results from activity_log inspected. Original turn content cross-checked against MCP fields.
No analysis of 3B retry cost (wasted tokens on double-failure). No analysis of whether 3B→30B fallback is cheaper than direct 30B extract.
No end-to-end test of extract → activity_log → review_consumer → 27B verify flow. Only structural DB/code inspection.
No comparison of different P-R-J model assignments. The review_pipeline_3model.py uses specific models but the evaluation assumes this assignment is optimal without testing alternatives.

disagreement_with_27b.detail: The evaluation should include token accounting. Example: 3B double-failure at ~100 tokens/fact + 30B full rewrite = ~300 tokens wasted per fallback. At 4681 unprocessed turns with 50% fallback rate, that's ~702K wasted tokens.

The pipeline has only processed 4 turns. To establish a valid baseline, we need to process at least 50+ turns end-to-end and measure: total processing time, total tokens, per-turn breakdown, 3B success rate, 30B fallback rate.

Current assignment: P=R1-8B(:8083), R=Qwen7B(:8080), J=Selene(:8081). Alternative: P=Qwen3-4B(:8082), R=Qwen30B(:8080), J=Qwen7B(:8080). Or: all roles via single model with different prompts. These should be compared.
32B is more conservative due to lack of empirical data. With only 4 processed turns, confidence cannot exceed 70.

cost_projection.bottleneck: 30B fallback takes ~28 min for 2340 turns. 3B processes faster per turn but wastes tokens on retries.

recommendations.action: Run end-to-end pipeline on 50+ turns to collect actual metrics (not projections)
recommendations.detail: Call extract_pipeline.py --limit 50, measure: total_time, per-turn latency, 3B vs 30B tokens, fallback rate, faithfulness %.
Track prompt_tokens, completion_tokens per LLM call. Store in review_facts + activity_log body.

recommendations.action: Test alternative 3B→30B strategy for long turns
recommendations.detail: For T>500ch turns, skip 3B retry and go direct to 30B. Compare success rate and total tokens against current 3B double-attempt approach.
Run review_pipeline_3model.py with different assignments on same extract data. Measure: total tokens, review quality, time.
